extracted.intended_audience: authors submitting life-science research manuscripts to Review Commons (preprint-based peer review)
extracted.subtask_description: Author-facing guidelines for submitting life-science research manuscripts to the Review Commons platform, covering scope and initial editorial assessment, mandatory preprint posting, the peer-review workflow, transfer to affiliate journals, scooping protection, and appeals/challenges.

rubrics_metrics.name: Mandatory posting of the preprint
rubrics_metrics.description: Review Commons requires all authors to post their manuscript on a preprint server at submission (recommended: bioRxiv or medRxiv). As of July 1, 2023, Review Commons will only peer review manuscripts for which a preprint is publicly available.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Recommended route: post to bioRxiv/medRxiv then transfer; alternative: submit directly to Review Commons which can post to bioRxiv (technical reasons prevent automatic posting to medRxiv via the direct route). Posting a preprint at submission is a mandatory condition for peer review on the platform and is tied to scooping protection offered by affiliate journals.

rubrics_metrics.name: Unpublished / not under consideration requirement
rubrics_metrics.description: Submitting a preprint or a manuscript for peer-review by Review Commons implies that it reports unpublished work and that neither it, nor parts of it, have been published or are under consideration for publication in a journal.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Authors must ensure the work is original and not concurrently submitted elsewhere; submission to Review Commons signals exclusivity with respect to journal consideration (though the preprint may be public).

rubrics_metrics.name: No journal-format requirement
rubrics_metrics.description: There is no need to comply with a particular journal format to submit to Review Commons.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Authors can submit in their preferred manuscript format; they do not need to reformat to match any downstream journal before initial peer review on Review Commons.

rubrics_metrics.name: Scope of Review Commons
rubrics_metrics.description: The scope covered includes a wide range of life-science areas: biotechnology, synthetic biology and methods; cell biology; development; computational biology and bioinformatics; systems biology and systems medicine; genes, genomes, epigenetics, RNA and chromatin; immunology; microbiology; molecular medicine and disease; molecular physiology; neuroscience; plant biology; protein structure and function; biophysics & biochemistry; evolution & ecology.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Manuscripts must fall within these topical areas to be considered for peer review. The initial editorial assessment will verify topical fit.

rubrics_metrics.name: Only research papers accepted
rubrics_metrics.description: Only research papers are considered (no reviews/commentaries/editorials).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Non-research article types should not be submitted; Review Commons is limited to primary research reports.

rubrics_metrics.name: Completeness of methods, data and manuscript sections
rubrics_metrics.description: Manuscripts must have fully-described materials & methods, fully described data figures, comprehensive references and rigorous introduction, results, and conclusions.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Initial assessment requires sufficient methodological and data detail so that expert reviewers can evaluate the work thoroughly. Incomplete methods or poorly described figures may lead to rejection at editorial assessment.

rubrics_metrics.name: Availability of expert reviewers
rubrics_metrics.description: Initial assessment includes whether there is a reasonable likelihood that expert reviewers will be available to conduct a thorough review of the study.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If suitable expert reviewers cannot be reasonably identified, the manuscript may not be sent for peer review.

rubrics_metrics.name: Sufficient advance / informativeness of reviews
rubrics_metrics.description: The study should represent a sufficient advance in the field such that the resulting public reviews will be informative and helpful to other researchers.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Review Commons favors manuscripts where peer review will produce reviews of broad interest/value; very incremental work that would not yield informative public reviews may be declined.

rubrics_metrics.name: Ethics, biosecurity and scientific integrity screening
rubrics_metrics.description: Review Commons reserves the right to reject manuscripts at any point if ethical, biosecurity or scientific integrity issues arise. In serious cases, Review Commons may post a note of editorial concern next to the public reviews.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Manuscripts raising such concerns can be rejected at any stage; the platform may flag issues publicly alongside reviews to alert readers and downstream journals.

rubrics_metrics.name: Referee selection principles
rubrics_metrics.description: Referee selection is based on a balance of factors, including expertise, scientific reputation, and our previous experience with the referee. Review Commons will strive for a balance of seniority, gender and geographical location.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Authors may recommend referees; they may also request exclusion of specific referees and Review Commons will comply with exclusion requests. Referee recommendations are considered but are not binding on the editor.

rubrics_metrics.name: Reviewer anonymity and transparent peer review
rubrics_metrics.description: Referee reports will remain anonymous unless the referees sign the reports. Referee reports will be posted alongside the published article and/or preprint (‘Transparent Peer Review’).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: By default referees are anonymous, but they may sign if they choose. Reports will be made public alongside the (peer-reviewed) preprint or published article when transferred to an affiliate journal.

rubrics_metrics.name: Cross-commenting among referees
rubrics_metrics.description: Before the referee reports are sent to authors, they will be circulated in anonymized form to all referees such that referees can cross-comment on each other’s analysis. The resulting comments, if any, will be included in the reports forwarded to the authors and to the selected target journal.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Referees see anonymized versions of other reviews and may add cross-comments; this can strengthen and clarify the set of reports sent to authors.

rubrics_metrics.name: No confidential comments to the editor
rubrics_metrics.description: Review Commons does not allow ‘confidential comments to the editor’.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: All substantive referee feedback should be in the reports that may be made public; referees cannot submit private confidential notes for editors only.

rubrics_metrics.name: Exclusion of unprofessional reviews
rubrics_metrics.description: The Managing Editor has the right to exclude reviews that are deemed unprofessional in tone or content.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Editors will screen referee reports for professionalism and may withhold reports that fail tone/content standards before forwarding to authors or making public.

rubrics_metrics.name: Posting of reviews and authors' response upon transfer
rubrics_metrics.description: Review Commons will post the reviews and the authors’ response on bioRxiv or medRxiv when the authors transfer their manuscript to the first affiliate journal. The reviews and the authors’ response will appear alongside the peer reviewed preprint.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: When authors move to an affiliate journal, the complete peer-review package (reports + response) is made public with the preprint to provide transparent peer review for readers and downstream journals.

rubrics_metrics.name: Communication of reviews to external journals requires reviewer agreement
rubrics_metrics.description: If authors wish to submit their manuscript to a journal outside of the consortium of affiliate journals, the manuscript should be formally withdrawn from consideration by Review Commons. Review Commons will communicate the reviews to external journals only in agreement with the reviewers.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Authors cannot unilaterally transfer reviews to non-affiliate journals without reviewers' consent; formal withdrawal and reviewer agreement are required for external sharing.

rubrics_metrics.name: Review challenge procedure — limited grounds for appeal
rubrics_metrics.description: Authors can formally request for a specific report to be withdrawn or amended before making the reviews public and transferring the manuscript to an affiliate journal. Such requests should be addressed to the editors with a detailed description of the reasons motivating the challenge.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Editors will only consider challenges in exceptional cases involving clearly inappropriately worded content. Scientific disagreement or controversies about interpretation, novelty or significance are not sufficient grounds for challenge. When an appeal is considered, editors will offer a call and will decide in consultation with the Advisory Board or other reviewers when necessary.

rubrics_metrics.name: Revision templates and indication of revision intent (REVISION PLAN vs FULL REVISION)
rubrics_metrics.description: Authors should use one of two template documents to indicate how the manuscript should be considered by affiliate journals: REVISION PLAN (to delineate planned revisions) or FULL REVISION (only if the submitted manuscript is an already fully revised manuscript in response to reviewers).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Selecting the correct template is important because it informs affiliate editors whether they are receiving a preliminary revision with a plan or a fully revised manuscript. Review Commons editors will not advise on which revision would be required for publication in affiliate journals.

rubrics_metrics.name: Recommended initial response period (4 weeks) and extensions
rubrics_metrics.description: Authors have a recommended four weeks to prepare an initial response to reviewers in the form of a revision plan, as well as a preliminary revision of the manuscript. Extensions are possible if authors prefer to undertake major revisions that include additional experimentation.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The short period is intended for addressing presentation issues and minor revisions; authors may request more time for substantive work.

rubrics_metrics.name: Recipient journal response timeline (10 working days)
rubrics_metrics.description: Upon transfer, the recipient journal will have 10 working days to respond with an editorial decision to authors; this may be 'reject', 'accept as is/with minor changes', or 'expression of interest to publish subject to revision'.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The decision may include explicit statements about required revisions, including possible additional experiments. Authors should expect a rapid initial response from affiliate journals.

rubrics_metrics.name: Affiliate journals' obligations regarding re-review and referee contact
rubrics_metrics.description: Affiliate journals have agreed not to review the manuscripts afresh with a new set of reviewers. A target journal may ask for additional expert advice to arbitrate on issues raised or to obtain complementary evaluations. The target journal will receive the identity of the reviewers. Affiliated journals are encouraged to only contact referees where this is required for an informed editorial process and not to request an editorial opinion on journal fit.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: While journals should rely principally on the Review Commons review file, they may seek targeted additional input. Reviewers' identities are shared with the target journal upon transfer.

rubrics_metrics.name: No parallel transfers; manuscript locking; transfer limits
rubrics_metrics.description: Parallel transfers to multiple journals are not possible. The manuscript will remain in a 'locked' stage on the Review Commons system while it is under consideration at an affiliate journal. Authors are encouraged to limit their transfers to four journals.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This prevents simultaneous submissions to multiple affiliate journals. Partner journals are not informed of the manuscript's submission history except in specific ethics/integrity cases or when a manuscript is rejected after revision and re-reviewed.

rubrics_metrics.name: Authors may take refereed preprint to non-affiliate journals (with conditions)
rubrics_metrics.description: Authors can decide to take their refereed preprint to any journal outside of the affiliate journals. In such a case, the editor of that journal can approach the platform for the referee names and referee reports.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: To submit to a non-affiliate journal, authors should formally withdraw from Review Commons; communication of reports to external editors requires agreement with reviewers (see above).

rubrics_metrics.name: Scooping protection for affiliate journals
rubrics_metrics.description: All affiliate journals apply an extended scooping protection policy: manuscripts reviewed by Review Commons are protected against scooping by competing publications from the date of posting of the cognate preprint to bioRxiv/medRxiv, provided the manuscript was submitted to the journal within 4 months of posting the preprint.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The policy guarantees that a competing paper published after posting the preprint will not constitute grounds for potential rejection by affiliate journals. Scooping protection does NOT apply to related papers with an overlapping set of authors.

rubrics_metrics.name: Review Commons Rapid Commitment (RC-RC) option
rubrics_metrics.description: Authors can opt into RC-RC during submission. If the manuscript is declined by two affiliate journals, Review Commons will consult with Life Science Alliance and FEBS Open Bio to assess suitability; if of interest, these editors will provide a commitment within 48 hours with specific feedback on what would be required for publication.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Authors who opt in are under no obligation to accept any offer; the RC-RC is intended to help find a suitable journal rapidly when initial affiliate journals decline.
